t: Section 12B (d) of the Federal Reserve Act, as amended (U. S. C,. title 12, sec. 264 (d)), is hereby repealed.

fable.w: This section only repeals a subsection of the Federal Reserve Act. It sets up no comment period, hearing, advisory body, consultation with outside parties, rulemaking authority, or right to sue. There is no real tempting reading, since no party outside the federal government is involved in any federal decision.
fable.s: Section 12B (d) of the Federal Reserve Act, as amended (U. S. C,. title 12, sec. 264 (d)), is hereby repealed.

qwen_block.w: This section simply repeals a previous statutory provision. It does not establish any new process for consultation, public comment, advisory committees, or coordination with outside parties. It is a legislative amendment that removes existing law, not a mechanism for participation.
qwen_block.s: Section 12B (d) of the Federal Reserve Act, as amended (U. S. C,. title 12, sec. 264 (d)), is hereby repealed.

opus.w: The section only repeals a subsection of the Federal Reserve Act. It does not create or require any consultation, comment period, hearing, advisory body, rulemaking or right to sue involving people outside the federal government. Whatever the repealed subsection once said, this text creates no process for outsiders to take part in a federal decision.
opus.b:
1. **Tempting reading:** Someone might guess that the repealed subsection, 12 U.S.C. 264(d) (part of the old FDIC provisions in Section 12B of the Federal Reserve Act), included some procedure involving outside parties. That reading fails because the text here only repeals it. It names no outside party, consultation, hearing, rulemaking or right to sue, so nothing in it brings anyone outside the federal government into a federal decision.
